issue_context.title: Create an IQueueDataHandler / IDataDownloader implementation for Polygon API.
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
[Polygon.io](https://polygon.io/docs/#getting-started) provides affordable market data via API. It would be nice to have this supported in LEAN. Their API can support historical download and live data.

#### Actual Behavior
No Polygon implementation.

#### Potential Solution
Implement Polygon.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
comments: @jaredbroad which polygon endpoints would you like implemented i.e. stocks, forex, crypto or all of them? Would like to try to sort this issue.
Thanks @mul1sh; I'd shoot for those 3 -"stocks, forex, crypto" - I think Polygon's API is abstracted enough.
Looks like Alpaca uses plygon.io , so part of that implementation is already there.  But would love to be able to do backtesting with data from polygon.io

I tried using the LEAN toolbox for a local installation with Polygon.IO as my data stream, and it fails.   Has anyone done a complete development of the APIs that can easily be used ?    Is there still a bounty available ?

I need to have a local installation that I can very easily download the data and store properly in the LEAN format.

I can write all the code for this, but it would be nice if someone has already implemented the data handler robustly.

Also, there doesn't seem to be support for weekends where Polygon.IO serves a 404 error and the LEAN toolbox terminates on:

20201122 08:16:14.720 ERROR:: PolygonDownloaderProgram.PolygonDownloader():  System.Net.WebException: The remote server returned an error: (404) Not Found.

Also, the conditions mappings and exchange were not fully implemented in the PolygonDataQueueHandler.cs

yield return new Tick(time, request.Symbol, string.Empty, string.Empty, row.BidSize, row.BidPrice, row.AskSize, row.AskPrice);
